name: veterinary_clinic_system_030_revenue_by_location_rollup
instruction: Run the month-end revenue and accounts-receivable aging report by billing location as of the episode date. For each location, push one ops_reports row with report='revenue_by_location' and the live batch_code, containing: location_id, location_name, paid_revenue (sum of amount_paid on paid, non-draft invoices at that billing location), open_receivables (sum of total_amount - amount_paid on sent or overdue, non-draft invoices at that billing location), invoice_count (all non-draft invoices at that location), ar_aging (dict current/days_1_30/days_31_60/days_61_90/days_90_plus; each bucket is the portion of open_receivables whose invoice due_date falls in that bucket relative to the episode date, with boundaries inclusive at the low end and exclusive at the high end), distinct_patient_count (distinct patient_id values on non-draft invoices at that location), top_delinquent_patient_id, top_delinquent_patient_name, top_delinquent_owner_id, top_delinquent_owner_name, top_delinquent_open_amount (the open invoice with the largest unpaid balance at that location, or nulls when there is no open receivable), and provider_count (providers assigned to that location). The aging buckets must sum exactly to open_receivables. Exclude draft invoices and billing estimates entirely. Use the invoice's billing location for grouping, not the patient's home location. Also append one audit_log row (action='REVENUE_REPORT', actor='system', actor_role='system', target_collection='ops_reports', target_id=batch_code, details containing the batch code, occurred_at=episode timestamp) documenting the report run. If report or audit rows for this batch already exist, overwrite them.

success_criteria.summary: One ops_reports row per location (report='revenue_by_location') with paid_revenue, open_receivables, invoice_count, ar_aging buckets summing to open_receivables, distinct_patient_count, top delinquent patient/owner, and provider_count, plus one summary row (report='revenue_by_location_summary') with total_paid_revenue, total_open_receivables, total_invoice_count, and location_count. All derived from billing_invoices joined to locations, owners, patients and providers. Draft invoices and billing_estimates are excluded. One audit_log row per batch documenting the run. Dual-path verification (Python filter vs SQL GROUP BY/SUM/CASE) for every aggregate and every aging bucket. All other collections unchanged.

checks.expect: Exactly 3 revenue_by_location detail rows and 1 revenue_by_location_summary row for this batch, all derived fields correct and aging buckets summing to open_receivables
Exactly one new REVENUE_REPORT row for this batch
paid_revenue, open_receivables, invoice_count, distinct_patient_count, and every aging bucket agree between a raw-row Python filter and an independent SQL aggregate

hazards: Draft invoice at location 3 (billing_invoices.id=3, invoice_number=INV-1003, status='draft', total_amount=546) must be excluded from every revenue, open-receivable, invoice-count, and patient-count aggregate; a solution that includes 'unpaid' or 'non-paid' invoices without explicitly dropping drafts inflates location 3's open_receivables by $546.

The only open invoices are billing_invoices.id=1 (location 1, due 2026-08-21, status 'sent') and id=2 (location 2, due 2026-09-20, status 'sent'); there are no 'overdue' status rows in the seed snapshot. An agent that only treats status='overdue' as open receivable will produce $0 open_receivables and miss both aging buckets.

Aging is driven by due_date against the episode date (base 2026-09-30, jitter ±3 days), not by status. Invoice 1 is 37-43 days past due and therefore always falls in the days_31_60 bucket; invoice 2 is 7-13 days past due and therefore always in days_1_30. Hardcoding a bucket or using issued_date instead of due_date gives plausible-but-wrong numbers.

Grouping must use billing_invoices.location_id, not patients.location_id. Patient 2 has home location 1 but appears on a location-2 invoice; an agent that joins through patients.location_id will mis-assign that open receivable and produce a wrong top delinquent for location 2.

owner.balance is a decoy: owner 1 balance is $134 but open invoice is $523, owner 2 balance is $0 but open invoice is $214. The top delinquent account must be derived from the unpaid invoice, not the owner balance field.
Items are duplicated across locations (e.g., Buprenorphine at locations 1 and 2); the report must be one row per location, not per item, and the key is location_id.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Fuses revenue rollup, AR aging, and multi-hop delinquent-account resolution into a single report. Requires strict draft exclusion, sent/overdue open-receivable handling, due-date-driven aging buckets, invoice billing location (not patient home location), and dual-path SQL-vs-Python verification of every aggregate. No off-the-shelf veterinary PMS report task combines all of these constraints with adversarial decoy rows.
